scores.why: Ten sheets meet the limit, but repeated summaries and sheet 9’s roughly 768 words outside collapsed details weaken presentation discipline.

fixes.change: Keep the proposition, short A/B comparison and creative-lead decision visible; place the insight, extended rationale, specifications and readiness checklist in expandable reference sections.
Remove this repeated summary: the headline, opening paragraph and metric tiles already communicate its three points.

scores.why: The essential evidence, deliverables, usage, risks and owners are present, but the approval request leaves pilot effort and operating-cost estimation without an explicit owner or deadline.

fixes.quote: Pilot effort and operating costs are still to be estimated.
fixes.change: Add a visible action assigning management and the operator to estimate pilot effort, subscription and support costs before live-use approval.

fixes.quote: Targets: question precision >80%, draft survival >70%, review <30 minutes; Greek-language quality and voluntary adoption.
fixes.change: Add the six-project retrospective sample and the week-4 stop rule beside these targets so the sponsor can understand the approval conditions without opening the ledger.

scores.why: The AI/code/people distinction is strong, but several executive-facing phrases retain technical shorthand or awkward wording.

fixes.quote: Targets: question precision >80%, draft survival >70%, review <30 minutes; Greek-language quality and voluntary adoption.
fixes.change: Use ‘Over 80% of questions judged useful; over 70% of draft text retained; under 30 minutes of review,’ followed by the language and adoption measures.

fixes.quote: Signed as the account lead’s was: in the run, by a named person, due before week 4 goes live.
fixes.change: Replace with ‘The creative lead must record a named evaluation before week 4; creative output remains in shadow mode.’

scores.why: The answer-first opening and evidence-to-decision sequence work, but the last two titles dilute their takeaways with qualifications and an unsupported deadline promise.

fixes.quote: The creative drafts stayed inside the signed-off facts and the spec table, except three things to strike and one call for the creative lead.
fixes.change: Replace with ‘Creative drafts still need a creative lead: three corrections and one judgement call.’

fixes.quote: Approve the four-week pilot: usage is measured in tokens, the cost of running it is not yet, and week 1 settles both.
fixes.change: Replace with ‘Approve a conditional four-week pilot; confirm capacity and operating costs before live use,’ aligning the title with the actual decision gates.

scores.why: Brief Builder has a clear promise, anatomy and human gate, but its operating principles and practical handover are less prominent than its internal pipeline.

fixes.quote: Ask, don’t guess · Surface, don’t resolve · Flag, don’t correct · Look up, don’t invent · Sign, don’t send
fixes.change: Move this compact principles statement out of the ledger and place it beside the pipeline.

fixes.quote: Code checks citations and gates the run; static review pages support command-line operation.
fixes.change: Replace with a concrete workflow: the operator runs the folder, the account lead reviews and records approval, and two trained brief champions take over by week 4.

scores.why: The source defines a distinctive, coherent editorial system, but oversized supporting elements and an uneven creative composition weaken hierarchy; full rendered inspection was unavailable.

fixes.change: Reduce the 24px role legend to a compact horizontal key on desktop, retaining a stacked version on phones.
Integrate the can into a deliberate desktop composition with the square and vertical artwork instead of placing a 40%-width plate alone on a second row.

scores.why: Headline tokens, model IDs, timings, costs, checks and sign-off match the artifacts, but small residual claims misdescribe the artwork and equate agent attempts with individual model calls.

fixes.quote: Clear space of one wordmark height kept free on every side of the name; ring, leaf and name sit in the central column so the 9:16 crop clips nothing
fixes.change: Replace ‘ring, leaf’ with the actual wind stroke and bubbles, and limit any clearance claim to applications that have been measured.

fixes.quote: Nine model calls (four documents, one sent back once).
fixes.change: Use ‘Nine model-agent attempts, each potentially containing multiple turns (four documents, one retried).’ Apply the same terminology in the ledger.

scores.why: Navigation, focus handling and offline dependencies are thoughtfully implemented, but phone ordering separates important qualifications from the content they explain and the mobile contents control competes with ten progress ticks.

fixes.change: Keep the ‘Three strikes, one call’ warning immediately before the creative proposition on phones rather than after the entire creative brief.
Hide progress ticks below 700px and reserve the centre navigation area for a stable sheet counter and Contents button.

scores.why: The artwork is appealing, honestly labelled and uses the supplied specifications, but the can infringes wordmark clearance and the vertical execution knowingly leaves the brand lockup in the caption zone.

fixes.change: Increase the gaps above and below the wordmark to at least one wordmark height; the inspected raster places both the yellow symbol and category line too close.

fixes.quote: 9:16 still frame at the TikTok in-feed spec; the lockup sits in TikTok’s caption zone, a dedicated 9:16 layout would raise it
fixes.change: Provide that dedicated vertical composition now, raising the lockup while retaining the mock-up label and provisional specification caveat.

overall: Strong evidence-led deliverable, but not ready to ship unchanged: tighten the presentation layer, complete the pilot approval conditions and refine the creative applications. Hash verified; no repository files changed. Chrome failed to launch through both attempted methods, so visual and UX scores rely on HTML/CSS/JavaScript inspection and direct inspection of the embedded can.
